$schema_note: User-visible product improvements, newest first. Feeds the pipeline's What's-new card and the homepage footer's latest-improvement stamp — one source, both surfaces (the homepage must match the real site). Keep entries honest, dated, and user-phrased; trim to ~12.

entries.title: Market briefs show full bedroom rents and their provenance
entries.blurb: Where the research carries a full FY2026 row — LA's Federal-Register revision, San Francisco's housing-authority sheet, Newark's state-treasury table — the brief now lists 0BR through 3BR with a verified/sourced chip, and prints the provenance note under the figure: where the number came from, and what was rejected on the way.

entries.title: Break it yourself: the return engine, live on the homepage
entries.blurb: A new interactive band puts three levers — exit cap, rent growth, vacancy — in your hands and recomputes IRR, equity multiple, cash-on-cash, exit value and NOI on every tick, through the same deterministic engine that prices real screens. Runs entirely in your browser on the labeled sample deal; no AI in the box.

entries.title: Compare shows each deal's leverage spread
entries.blurb: The side-by-side view gains a 'Leverage vs 30-yr' row — the signed spread between each deal's going-in cap and the freshest 30-yr fixed, color-coded negative / thin / positive with the same arithmetic as the deal page, captioned with the benchmark and its as-of date.

entries.title: The price ticker carries every covered market's FY2026 rent
entries.blurb: All fourteen sourced FY2026 2BR fair-market rents now ride the dark ticker — derived from the research layer, each linking to its market brief, with the DC metro's shared figure riding once instead of four times. The proof strip's sector count is computed now too; the typed-in number had drifted.

entries.title: Every covered market now carries its FY2026 fair-market rent
entries.blurb: A sourced HUD FY2026 2BR fair-market rent now backs 17 of 18 metro entries — San Francisco straight from the housing authority's own sheet, North Jersey from the state's republication of HUD's tables, LA from the April revision in the Federal Register. Seattle stays an honest gap: the widely-quoted figure turned out to be average rent, not the FMR.

entries.title: The demo shows the leverage check; Compare names covered markets
entries.blurb: The sample screen now runs the same leverage arithmetic every real deal gets, and the side-by-side Compare view carries a covered-market row — all three deal surfaces agree on scope.

entries.title: Every deal gets a leverage check against today's 30-yr rate
entries.blurb: The deal page now computes the spread between the going-in cap and the freshest FRED 30-yr fixed — negative leverage and thin spreads called out in plain numbers, sourced and dated. Arithmetic, not an opinion.

entries.title: The screen absorbs a 101-page crash post-mortem
entries.blurb: Negative leverage named outright, stabilized occupancy above ~95% challenged, exit values checked for the 'there's always a buyer' myth and missing sale costs, and demand claims weighed against supply — disciplines drawn from the industry's most famous lessons-learned memo.

entries.title: The challenger learned the down-cycle classics
entries.blurb: Assumption challenges now overlay the discipline every crash re-teaches: market-driven leasing assumptions, worst-case drift, cash flow over exit hopes, and no credit for 'other buyers are circling'.

entries.title: Stale pages now fix themselves
entries.blurb: If your browser is showing an older copy of the site, it now notices the newer build and reloads itself once — no hard refresh needed, ever again.

entries.title: Every ticker figure is a door
entries.blurb: The dark price ticker's items — FMRs, rent caps, the 30-yr rate — now click through to the market behind them, with a caption saying what the band is.

entries.title: Market briefs open without an account
entries.blurb: Clicking a market in the homepage band used to hit a login wall. The 15 covered-market briefs — rules, rents, coverage — are now public; your own deal memory still needs a sign-in.
